- When sentiment is consistently negative or low (e.g., 0.00–0.33), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 15–30% for next 3–5 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 3x recent mean), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 2x recent peak or 1.5x prior 7-day average.  
- If sentiment is positive and price is trending down, model often fails to mean-revert; add a 1–2 day lag correction to align with sentiment reversal.  
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.33–0.67), model tends to overreact to short-term volatility; apply smoothing filter (e.g., 3-day moving average) to forecast.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the period; apply downward bias of 10–20% for first 7–10 days if sentiment is weak or mixed.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., 0.67 → 0.00 → 0.67), model tends to mispredict direction; use sentiment momentum as a lagged indicator for 1–2 day correction.
